summary: Auth: attempts to fix a crash when creating a user without a password (e.g. users auto-provisioned on first sign-in via the auth provider, UserRegister(email=...)) by passing password=None instead of bytes(None); also makes the login model's password optional and modernises type hints. But dispatch_user.password is NOT NULL (models.py DispatchUser.password nullable=False), so creation now fails with a database NotNullViolation instead (get_or_create swallows it and returns no user); upstream fixed this next in 82e9444 'Fixes NotNullViolation on user creation'.

statements.why: This is a login/user-creation change that doesn't work: a None password hits DispatchUser.password nullable=False, so first-time users without a password (SSO/auto-provisioned via get_current_user -> get_or_create(UserRegister(email=...)), or /auth/register without password) still can't be created; get_or_create catches the IntegrityError and returns None. Login also now accepts a missing password field (safely rejected by verify_password).

statements.text: The agent also changed src/dispatch/auth/service.py, in a way plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: True but vacuous; also omits the auth/models.py change to login/registration models.

misses.what: The fix is incomplete: new users without a password (first sign-in through the auth provider, or registering without a password) still can't be created because the database requires a password; they get an error instead of an account.
Login/registration request models changed: password is now optional on login (missing password is just rejected as invalid credentials).
